newsitem.title: USA: L.A. utility sets $2.5 bln budget, up $70 mln.
newsitem.headline: L.A. utility sets $2.5 bln budget, up $70 mln.

text.p: The Los Angeles Board of Water and Power Commissioners Tuesday approved a $2.5 billion budget for fiscal 1997-98 (July-June) aimed at continued restructuring as competition is introduced into California's electric utility industry next year.
The new budget is about $70 million higher than the current budget, a spokesman for the municipal utility said.

"To be competitive by year 2003-04, the DWP's energy services business must lower the price of its product by generating $300 million annually for the next five years to contribute to debt reduction," Board Vice President Marcia Volpert said in a statement.
"This will require a mix of operating cost reductions, a reduction in the transfer of funds to the city and increased revenues," she added.
Volpert said the utility will cut about 1,500 staff positions from the energy side of operations in the coming fiscal year, which will trim annual costs by $90 million.
However, since these positions are currently occupied, funding must be provided in the new budget until the job cuts can be made through a targeted separation program.
The budget also reflects $78 million in non-labor reductions, or about 10 percent of discretionary expenditures in the energy services portion of the current budget.

For the $2 billion energy services budget, capital expenditures will be cut by $83 million, down 35 percent from the current year due to reduced additions and improvements to electric generation, distribution and general facilities.
About 65 percent of the capital program will be for distribution infrastructure and improvements for new business.
Energy services operation and maintenance is down $83 million or 17 percent, with all areas except marketing cut.
The $485 million water services budget includes a $19 million increase, primarily due to mandated water quality programs, and water reclamation.

In the five-year period beginning July 1, the water services capital expenditure program is expected to total $1.1 billion as the DWP complies with surface water treatment rules at local reservoirs and continues infrastructure improvements.
For fiscal 1997-98, the DWP anticipates it will provide a $106 million transfer to the city from electricity and water sales, a decrease of $11 million from the current year.
